justification: A's Reviewer_N9bU, at confidence 1, raised to accept on the rebuttal's framing and the promised de Haan citation, without new results or a proof check.

name: Reviewer expertise shaped clarity verdicts
justification: B's chair adopted the confidence-4 rfa1's verdict of 'clear', while A's chair took the density that aRng and N9bU reported as the main shortcoming.

name: One committee raised an issue the other missed
justification: Only A raised the correct, conceded point that the theory follows the authors' C-learning analysis, and the simple image tasks that the paper concedes.

name: Thin, unengaged review entered the decision
justification: B's Reviewer_xycR's 9 rested on assertion, with no engagement after the rebuttal, and counted unchallenged in a two-sentence meta-review.

name: Enthusiastic low-confidence review carried weight
justification: B's Reviewer_xycR gave the only 9 of seven reviews on one paragraph of praise ('the work is solid') and one minor comment, which lifted B's mean.

name: Award tier assigned without a stated case
justification: B's meta-review is two sentences ('well-received ... discussion strengthened the acceptance score') and gives no reason for the oral tier.

name: Only one committee's reviewers knew the baseline literature
justification: Only A's Reviewer_yauQ knew the closely related C-learning work, checked the theory's novelty against it and asked for that baseline; B's reviewers took the comparisons as 'comprehensive'.

name: Reviewer moved after reading the other reviews
justification: B's Reviewer_LgSM raised to 8 'after reading the other reviews and the authors' responses to them', with no new evidence; the reply to LgSM was only a promise.

name: New results shown to one committee only
justification: Only A, in answer to Reviewer_yauQ, got a new C-learning-variant result (about 0.07 against 0.2 return), and yauQ raised; B never saw it.

name: Committees scored similar assessments on different scales
justification: B's careful reviews are no more favourable than A's (B's Reviewer_6QWr wrote 'very high quality' and gave 7), yet B's ratings run higher, partly from a 9 on generic praise.

name: Narrow-audience objection capped one committee's tier
justification: A's chair limited the 'rather significant impact' to 'some domains', a breadth limit that fits its poster; B raised no breadth concern.

name: One committee raised an issue the other missed
justification: Only B raised the Algorithm 2 flaw, the single-tree theory versus forest experiments, the missing d > 2 theorem and the database-histogram work; only A raised the coordinate swap and the shrinking gain over uniform sampling.

name: Thin, unengaged review entered the decision
justification: B's Reviewer_1UMR rated 8 on two sentences, did not check the math, never joined the discussion, and the score counted unchallenged.

name: Enthusiastic low-confidence review carried weight
justification: B's Reviewer_1UMR gave the only 8 in either committee at confidence 2 on a two-sentence review with no weaknesses, lifting B's ratings toward the oral.

name: Area chair set the award above reviewers' scores
justification: B's chair gave an oral on 4, 7, 7, 8 (mean 6.5) with no reviewer arguing for an oral, citing an 'absolutely above the bar' judgement found in no public review.

name: Committee discounted a known substantive flaw
justification: B's ybbQ found a real Algorithm 2 flaw the rebuttal skipped, and nDd9's single-tree versus forest gap was conceded, yet B's meta-review weighed neither and gave an oral.

name: Award tier assigned without a stated case
justification: B's meta-review states novelty above the bar but writing 'almost ... unpublishable' and asks for polishing; it argues only for acceptance and gives no case for an oral.

name: Only one committee's reviewers knew the baseline literature
justification: B's reviewers named specific prior work (database histograms, R-trees, Feldman-Langberg) and checked novelty against it, while A's QFcb only noted the missing related-work section without naming it.

name: One committee raised an issue the other missed
justification: Only A's h23K raised that Theorem 2's surrogate set reduces the problem to the MGT loop, a checkable depth concern B never weighed.

name: Thin, unengaged review entered the decision
justification: A's yA7o spent 2 hours, checked no proofs, asked for experiments on a theory paper, and its update named no specific gap, yet its 6 counted unchallenged.

name: Committees weighted the same weakness differently
justification: Both saw missing experiments and dense notation; A's yA7o held experiments against the paper and A's chair called it 'very difficult to follow', while B's kvzq excused experiments and B treated notation as fixable.

name: Area chair set the award above reviewers' scores
justification: B's chair chose an oral on 8/7/6 with a top score of 'Top 50% of accepted' and no reviewer asking for an oral, on the chair's own reading.

name: Rebuttal moved scores in one committee only
justification: iUkv in B rose from 5 to 6 after the notation answers; no score in A moved.

name: Award tier assigned without a stated case
justification: B's meta-review justifies the oral with one generic sentence, 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution', and no case for an award tier.

name: Promised revisions credited by one committee only
justification: A's yA7o refused experiments and the continuous case put off as future work and A's chair still judged the paper hard to follow, while B credited promised notation fixes as making the problems fixable.

name: Committees held one paper type to different bars
justification: A's yA7o required experiments of an identification-theory paper, while B's kvzq said a theory paper should not be penalised for lacking them.

name: Rebuttal persuaded reviewers who could not check core
justification: B's iUkv could not follow the results or verify the proofs, yet rose from 5 to 6 on notation clarifications and promised revisions.

name: Narrow-audience objection capped one committee's tier
justification: A's 6Pv4 judged the paper better suited to a journal, one of A's grounds for a poster, while B raised no venue concern.

name: Unsure reviewers converged on marginal-accept scores
justification: R27 needs an invested champion and R36 an outweighed expert; neither names the mechanism here, where a whole panel unable to check the core hedged at the same borderline score and the chair took that uniformity as the verdict.

name: One committee raised an issue the other missed
justification: Only A questioned why a Fourier series beats tanh or SignSwish (KUr5, FCVA), and A's AC required 'further justification'; no one in B raised this core-motivation doubt.

name: Thin, unengaged review entered the decision
justification: B's Reviewer_Xxt6 gave 8 after 2 hours with no stated weakness and posted no note after the rebuttal, and that 8 counted unchallenged toward the oral.

name: Committees weighted the same weakness differently
justification: Both committees flagged the missing ReActNet comparison and got the same +0.5 answer; A's AC kept it as a required revision, while B's AC called the rebuttal 'particularly good' and gave an oral.

name: Enthusiastic low-confidence review carried weight
justification: B's Reviewer_Xxt6 gave 8 after 2 hours, listed no weakness and called Fig. 1 'inspiring'; B's reviews mostly restate the paper's claims and lifted B's mean to 7.75.

name: Area chair set the award above reviewers' scores
justification: B's AC chose an oral although no reviewer rated above 8, on a personal reading ('I have gone through the paper by myself'), personal taste for 'a simple idea that works' and an impact claim no reviewer made.

name: Rebuttal moved scores in one committee only
justification: In B, Reviewer_f6JJ and Reviewer_oG66 raised scores after the response, while A's KUr5 kept 7 and no A score moved.

name: Reviewer moved after reading the other reviews
justification: B's Reviewer_oG66 raised to 8 'after reading comments from other reviewers', not on new evidence.

name: New results shown to one committee only
justification: Only B's f6JJ asked for the noise-only row; the authors gave it (77.16) with the ImageNet n_s and f6JJ raised to 7, while A never saw that result.

name: Committees scored similar assessments on different scales
justification: A's Reviewer_FCVA rated 6 on wholly positive text, while B rated 8/8/8/7 on reviews that mostly restate the paper and are less critical, so part of the gap is scoring leniency.
